facts.text: Owl staged the raid on Kuro's protectors as a deliberate plan to separate Kuro from his guardians and claim the divine heritage for himself.
Owl used bandits and Interior Ministry agents as cover to carry out his real objective during the raid.
When Wolf became too loyal and effective to fit Owl's plan, Owl wounded him mortally rather than killing him outright, intending for Kuro's blood heritage to do the rest.
Kuro found Wolf bleeding out in a burning temple and chose to share his blood with him, granting Wolf the dragon's heritage and binding their fates.
The gift of the dragon's heritage made Wolf unable to die, but the trauma of the event shattered his memory.
Wolf spent three years in a trance-like state at the bottom of a well in the Asha Reservoir, stripped of purpose and memory.
A woman named Emma, acting at the request of the dying Isshin Ashina, dropped a letter into the well telling Wolf that his master was alive and needed him.
Wolf climbed out of the well after receiving Emma's letter, beginning the game's story.
Wolf infiltrates Ashina Castle and finds Kuro imprisoned in a tower room by the Ashina clan.
Genichiro Ashina is Isshin Ashina's adoptive grandson and the current military leader of the Ashina domain.
Genichiro Ashina wants Kuro's blood to create an immortal army to save Ashina from the Interior Ministry's invasion.
On the bridge leaving Ashina Castle, Genichiro Ashina defeats Wolf decisively, severing Wolf's left arm at the elbow.
After losing his arm, Genichiro Ashina takes Kuro back into the castle, leaving Wolf for dead on the bridge.
Wolf does not die from his wounds because the dragon's heritage in his blood revives him, and he wakes in a dilapidated temple at the base of the mountain.
The Sculptor is an old man who saves Wolf and lives in a temple carving Buddhist statues compulsively.
The Sculptor gives Wolf a prosthetic arm to replace his severed limb.
The prosthetic arm was designed by Dogen, a physician and inventor, as a versatile tool platform rather than a simple replacement limb.

The prosthetic arm can be fitted with attachments including a grappling hook for traversal, a loaded axe for breaking shields, a flame vent for burning enemies, and a shield made from an ancient creature's shell for deflecting unblockable attacks.
The Sculptor's gift of the prosthetic arm is also the instrument he once used himself during his years as a shinobi.
Wolf fights through Ashina's outskirts, an army of soldiers, generals, and war beasts to reach the castle's main tower where Kuro and Isshin Ashina are located.
Isshin Ashina, elderly and dying, gives Wolf the name 'Sekiro, One-Armed Wolf' as an acknowledgment of his loyalty despite failure.
Dragon rot is a disease that spreads through the land every time Wolf dies and resurrects, draining the life force of people in his orbit.
Dragon rot manifests as a persistent wasting cough and gradual weakening, afflicting characters such as the Sculptor and Emma.
The dragon's heritage does not create life but borrows it, siphoning vitality from nearby living people to fuel Wolf's resurrection.
Kuro wants to sever the dragon's heritage because he has witnessed the suffering dragon rot causes to those around Wolf.
Rejuvenating sediment can cure dragon rot by drawing the disease out of the afflicted, but the cure is temporary and does not prevent future infection.
When an NPC is afflicted by dragon rot, their quest line freezes and their story content becomes inaccessible until cured.
Severing the dragon's heritage would end dragon rot but requires Wolf to die permanently.
Mount Kongo housed a monastery, Senpu Temple, where monks originally sought Buddhist enlightenment through meditation and scripture study.
The rejuvenating waters are especially concentrated on Mount Kongo because the mountain sits close to the source of the divine dragon's essence.
The monks of Senpu Temple began drinking the rejuvenating waters, which made them stronger and healthier, leading them to believe the waters were connected to enlightenment.
The monks of Senpu Temple abandoned Buddhist teachings and repurposed their meditation halls into laboratories to study the waters' effects.

The monks discovered that parasitic centipedes native to Mount Kongo, which lived in the rejuvenating waters, could act as conduits for the dragon's power and sustain a host body indefinitely if implanted in a human.
Monks willingly allowed centipedes to be inserted into their bodies, achieving a twisted immortality while losing their humanity.
Centipede-infested monks encountered at Senpu Temple move with unnatural, insectile motions and sometimes have visible centipedes protruding from their bodies.
The monks of Senpu Temple experimented on children from surrounding villages, attempting to turn them into artificial divine heirs carrying the dragon's heritage.
Most children used in the monks' experiments died because their bodies could not contain the forced dragon power, and the monks buried them in shallow graves on the mountainside.
One child, the Divine Child of Rejuvenation, survived the monks' experiments and stably carries a genuine fragment of the dragon's power.
The Divine Child of Rejuvenation is kept imprisoned in a shrine at Senpu Temple, worshipped by the monks as a living god while being denied freedom.
The Divine Child offers Wolf rice grown in Mount Kongo's soil infused with rejuvenating waters, which has a mild healing effect.
The Divine Child has studied ancient 'holy chapters' describing the dragon's original journey from the west, suggesting the journey can be reversed.
The Divine Child's plan, tied to the game's best ending, requires her to become a vessel for Kuro's soul and carry the heritage back across the sea to its origin.
Genichiro Ashina is portrayed as a patriot who loves Ashina and is desperate to save it from destruction by the Interior Ministry's invasion.
Genichiro Ashina plans to use Kuro's blood to create an immortal army to save Ashina from collapse.
Genichiro Ashina has been drinking the sacred rejuvenating sediment to enhance his body's strength, speed, and resilience, though it does not grant true immortality.
Isshin Ashina disapproves of Genichiro Ashina's obsession with immortality, believing that death gives life meaning and courage.
Isshin Ashina arranged for Emma to warn Wolf and helped set up Wolf's escape, all to protect Kuro from Genichiro Ashina's plans.
Genichiro Ashina trains in heretical arts forbidden by the Ashina School of Swordsmanship and acquires the Black Mortal Blade through unexplained means.
The Black Mortal Blade can open a gate to the underworld and pull the souls of the dead back into the world of the living, mirroring the Red Mortal Blade which can kill the immortal.
The Red Mortal Blade is obtained from Senpu Temple.

Wolf fights Genichiro Ashina three times: on the bridge, at the top of Ashina Castle, and in a final battle at a place called the Fountainhead/Silver field, each time showing further deterioration in Genichiro's methods and composure.
In the second fight at the top of Ashina Castle, Genichiro Ashina tears off his armor and wields a black-bladed bow charged with lightning.
In the final encounter, Genichiro Ashina uses the Black Mortal Blade to cut his own throat, sacrificing his body to open a gate that summons a young, resurrected Isshin Ashina from death.
Isshin Ashina, once resurrected by Genichiro Ashina's sacrifice, had already made peace with death and did not want to be brought back.
There are two distinct Great Serpents in Ashina, both once ordinary animals transformed over centuries by the rejuvenating waters into enormous, ancient beings.
The Great Serpents react to Wolf with hostility as if sensing that the dragon's heritage in his blood is related to the power within them.
The Sunken Valley is a deep, narrow gorge where sunlight reaches the bottom only briefly each day, and is home to the Sunken Valley Clan who worship the Great Serpents as gods.
The Sunken Valley Clan reject conventional Ashina society, fight with reckless abandon, and include warriors who use long-barreled rifles from cliffside positions.
The Gun Fort is the Sunken Valley Clan's stronghold, fortified into the cliffs and defended by gunfire.
The Long-armed Centipede Giraffe is a mini boss in the Gun Fort whose body is driven by an internal centipede parasite, causing rapid jerking windmill-like attacks.
The Guardian Ape is an enormous primate sustained unnaturally by the rejuvenating waters, guarding the Lotus of the Palace, an ingredient Kuro needs for the severance ritual.
After Wolf decapitates the Guardian Ape, its headless body rises again, picks up its severed head and a sword, and continues attacking, driven by a centipede parasite inside it.

The Guardian Ape has a mate, a second, less corrupted ape, who fights alongside the reanimated first ape in a hidden arena; when Wolf kills her, the headless first ape briefly cradles her body before resuming its attack.
